parole.significato: A (walnut- or poppy-seed) roll (similar to Swiss roll) traditionally eaten in Hungary at Christmas time or at Easter.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bavarian, compare Beugel, Beugl, Beigel (“a horseshoe-shaped walnut or poppy seed roll”), from German beugen (“to bend”). Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

parole.significato: backless kitchen stool, sometimes with a drawer for additional storage
parole.testo: From Bavarian hockerl (“small backless kitchen stool”), from German Hocker (“stool”) + -dli. Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

parole.significato: plump, chubby (having a full and rounded shape)
parole.testo: First attested in 1884. From Bavarian molet (“plump”), from German mollig, from Latin mollis (“soft”).
